Co-constraints fix OBX-2 to one exact value, which contradicts "accept both CE and CWE" and "responses SHOULD use CE". Every co-constraint row tests OBX-2 for an exact value (for example 'CE'). A submitter that sends CWE for a coded observation fails validation, although the narrative says systems SHALL accept both. Patient Condition (75323-6) is fixed to 'CWE' in Z22, Z32, and Z42, while every other coded observation is 'CE'. An IIS that follows the narrative's SHOULD (use CE in responses) fails Z32/Z42 validation for that observation. Free-text Comment (48767-8) is 'CE' in Z22 but 'ST' in Z32.
recommendation: Yes, it needs to be reflected (comment 28). Allow both CE and CWE where the narrative says both are accepted (a value-set check on OBX-2 instead of exact text), or narrow the narrative. Set 48767-8 to a text type (ST or TX) in every profile. Decide whether 75323-6 should be CE like the rest.

message: Newborn ('NB') names are not held to the family-and-given rule, and other names are over-constrained when an 'L' name is present. The profiles implement the two XPN flavors by slicing the whole PID segment on PID-5.7, not by name repetition. If any repetition is 'L', every repetition (nickname, maiden, and so on) must use XPN_IZ01 and have both family and given name. If no repetition is 'L', every repetition uses XPN_IZ02, where only one of family or given is needed, so an 'NB' placeholder name with one part passes. The two slice conditions also overlap: a patient with an 'L' and an 'N' name matches both. Slicing exists only in Z22; the response profiles (Z31, Z32) always use PID_IZ01 and Z42 uses PID_IZ02.
recommendation: Statement (2) exists: XPN.7 is R in every PID-5 flavor. Statement (1) holds for 'L' only. Ask IGAMT whether a slice or co-constraint can apply per repetition (by XPN.7). If not, use a conformance statement such as "each PID-5 repetition with XPN.7 in ('L','NB') SHALL value XPN.1 and XPN.2". Make the two slice conditions mutually exclusive. Decide whether responses should follow the same rule. Statement (3) has no counterpart in the narrative yet; the card should state it once the data type pages exist.

message: Patient conditions: the text uses 30945-0 in the no-vaccination group; the profiles only allow 75323-6 there. Section 4.8.6.2 says conditions are sent as 30945-0 (contraindication/precaution) observations in an ORC/RXA group that reports no vaccination. Section 4.4.4.4 and Figure 20 say patient conditions use 75323-6 in the Patient Observations group. The co-constraint tables follow 4.4.4.4: in the no-vaccination (CVX 998) group, 30945-0 is not allowed, and 75323-6 (with 85585-8 and 88878-4) is. 30945-0 is only allowed in the contraindicated group (NA with a real CVX).
recommendation: CDC decides which representation is current, then aligns sections 4.4.4.4 and 4.8.6, Figure 20, and the co-constraint tables.

message: IZ-41 and IZ-42 on the shared MSH flavor apply to every message, and no message can pass both. All eight profiles use one MSH flavor, MSH_#ConsolidatedIG_IZ01. It carries IZ-41 (MSH-16 SHALL be 'AL') and IZ-42 (MSH-15 SHALL be 'NE') as segment-level constraints, so both apply to VXU, QBP, ACK, and RSP alike. The drafted examples follow the usual pattern (VXU and QBP with MSH-15 'ER' and MSH-16 'AL'; ACK and RSP with 'NE'/'NE'), and every one fails one of the two. Z22 also has its own message-level IZ-41 with slightly different wording.
recommendation: Move the acknowledgment-type constraints to the message profiles that need them (for example, VXU and QBP: MSH-16 'AL'; ACK and RSP: MSH-15 and MSH-16 'NE'), and say in the narrative which values each message uses. The example checks skip IZ-41 and IZ-42 until this is fixed (quality/config.yml).

section_title: Use of Administered vs. Historical on Output
message: Text says RSP should leave RXA-9 empty; Z32 and Z42 require RXA-9 for completed doses. The narrative prefers an empty RXA-9 in responses. In Z32 and Z42, RXA-9 is conditional and becomes Required whenever RXA-20 is CP or PA, which is every administered or historical dose returned. An IIS that follows the preferred approach fails validation.
recommendation: CDC decides. Either change the response flavors to make RXA-9 O (or RE) in Z32/Z42, or replace the narrative's preference with what to send (for example, always '00' or '01').

section_title: Z42 - Return Evaluated Immunization History and Forecast
message: Z42's co-constraint table has no conditions, so every history dose needs a forecast group. Z22 and Z32 select a co-constraint table by the kind of Order Segment Group (administered, refused, …). Z42 has one unconditional table. Its "Immunization Forecast Results" group is R [1..*], so it applies to every ORC/RXA group in the response: each returned dose would need a forecast, and evaluation results are allowed in the forecast group. Z42 also has no rows for eligibility, funding, VIS, comments, or contraindications, which Z32 returns.
recommendation: Make the Z42 tables conditional like Z32: evaluation for administered or historical doses (RXA-20 CP or PA), and forecast for the CVX 998 group. Add the event-level observations that Z32 allows.

message: The Order Segment Group flavors (text and Figure 20) and the co-constraint tables do not match. The flavor sections and Figure 20 list which observations belong in each Order Segment Group. The co-constraint tables allow more in some places and less in others. Main differences: serological immunity, history of disease, and patient condition are allowed in the administered and historical event groups (the text puts them only in Patient Observations). In Z32 they are allowed in every group. The contraindication set is required in Figure 20 but optional in the tables. Indication observations are missing from the historical-event table. Z32, the history-only response, has evaluation and forecast groups. Z42 has a single table with no conditions (see the Z42 finding). The cell-by-cell comparison is on the comparison page.
recommendation: Agree with CDC which is intended, then align both. The text and Figure 20 are the more restrictive and readable statement, so the tables probably need to change. Once aligned, generate the figure from the co-constraint tables so they cannot drift apart again.

message: The refusal slice also requires RXA-6 = 999, which the refusal section does not list. The Z22 slicing selects the refusal flavor (RXA_IZ01_Ref) only when RXA-20 = 'RE' and RXA-6 = '999', and constraint IZ-48 requires RXA-6 = 999 whenever RXA-20 = 'RE'. The refusal section's list of minimum elements leaves out RXA-6. A refusal sent with any other amount is not validated against the refusal flavor (so RXA-18 is not checked as required) and fails IZ-48. The same applies to contraindicated (NA, CVX ≠ 998) and no-vaccination (NA, CVX 998) groups, which both also select on RXA-6 = 999.
recommendation: The slicing is set up consistently with IZ-45 and IZ-48. Add "RXA-6 = 999 – Administered amount" to the refusal list, and state the RXA-6/ORC-3 values in the non-administration sections too. Consider whether the slice should key on RXA-20 alone, so that a wrong RXA-6 is reported by IZ-48 rather than silently changing which flavor applies.

message: "A SNOMED CT code from PHVS_VaccinationContraindication_IIS", but 12 of the value set's 23 codes are not SNOMED CT. The value set mixes 11 SNOMED CT codes with 12 CDC PHIN VS (CDCPHINVS) codes. A sender can use a CDCPHINVS code and pass validation while breaking the narrative's SHALL; or follow the narrative and be unable to express the concepts that only have CDCPHINVS codes.
recommendation: Say "a code from the PHVS_VaccinationContraindication_IIS value set", or update the value set to SNOMED CT only.

section_title: Dose Validity and Reason for Validity
message: "Y or N are the only allowable values" for dose validity is not enforced. The dose-validity observation (59781-5) is typed ID with no value set in the Z32 and Z42 co-constraints, so any value passes.
recommendation: Bind OBX-5 for 59781-5 to HL70136_IZ01 (or an equivalent Y/N value set).

message: Forecast observations: the text and the Z42 table list different LOINC codes. The narrative allows the legacy 30979-9 (Vaccines Due Next) after 30956-7, but the Z42 forecast group has no row for it, so it cannot be sent. The Z42 forecast group allows 93123-8 and 93122-0, which the Forecast section (4.4.4.6) does not mention. The status observation 59783-1 is bound to Imm_status in Z32 but has no binding in Z42.
recommendation: Add 30979-9 to the forecast group (optional), describe 93123-8 and 93122-0 in 4.4.4.6, and bind 59783-1 in Z42.

message: ORC-12 (Ordering Provider) has usage C with no predicate. In ORC_IZ01 (Z22, Z32), ORC-12 is conditional, but there is no predicate, so neither readers nor validators know when it is required. Z42's ORC_IZ02 has it as O.
recommendation: Add the intended predicate, or set a fixed usage.

message: The text allows a time-zone offset in PID-7; the profiles reject one. PID-7 uses TS_NZ, whose time pattern (DTM_NZ) has no offset, so a birth date/time with an offset fails format validation. The narrative tells senders to use the birth time zone and tells IIS to ignore any offset present. RXA-3 and OBX-14 also use TS_NZ. Their wording ("use the local time zone") is consistent if it means local time without an offset.
recommendation: Say "local time of birth, without a time-zone offset" in the narrative. If offsets must be tolerated, loosen the flavor. Align Z42 with the other profiles.

message: "Use the CDCREC value set": the profiles bind category-only value sets, without MENA or the detailed codes. The narrative talks about "the CDCREC value set", including detailed subcategories and Middle Eastern or North African (MENA) as a top-level race category. The profiles bind PID-10 to PHVS_RaceCategory_CDC_NullFlavor (6 OMB categories, Other Race, and three unknown codes) and PID-22 to PHVS_EthnicityGroup_CDC_Unk. Neither contains MENA or any detailed code. Both are Static/Open, so a validator would likely only warn, but readers cannot see what is allowed.
recommendation: Name the bound value sets in the narrative (or rename them in IGAMT). Decide whether MENA and the detailed CDCREC codes belong in the binding (Dynamic), and whether 2131-1 Other Race remains.

message: "SHALL populate RXA-11" for administered doses, but the administered flavor has RXA-11 as RE. The narrative makes RXA-11 mandatory for administered vaccinations. In the administered flavor (RXA_IZ01_Adm) RXA-11 is RE, so a message without it passes validation. RXA-11.4 (Facility) is R within LA2_IZ01, which only applies when RXA-11 is sent.
recommendation: Make RXA-11 R in the administered flavor (and the RE side of the RXA_IZ01 predicate R), or soften the statement to SHOULD. With usage "R" now defined as "IIS reports an ERR if missing", R matches the intent.

message: Co-constraint tables use usage 'S', which the guide does not define. Eighteen co-constraint rows and groups have usage 'S' (for example, VIS groups, the contraindication group, and the forecast dates). The guide defines R, RE, O, C, X, and IX. A reader cannot tell whether 'S' means "should", "situational", or something else, and Figure 20 shows these items as Required.
recommendation: Define 'S' in this section (as IGAMT uses it), or replace it in the tables with a defined usage.
